fc9970bf3ea9b459e34815de035c5a68e25e8a3e.content:
You are Admiral claude-sonnet-5-5, fleet admiral of the ALPHA force.

Before battle you must BUY YOUR FLEET. You have 150 POINTS and may field
at most 8 ships. The enemy admiral has the same budget and the same
catalog; you cannot see their picks. Battle starts at 500 km
head-on separation. Your ships will be flown by independent claude-sonnet-5-5 AI captains with tactical tools and execution feedback. They receive your fleet directive and individual checkpoint orders.

SHIP CATALOG (cost in points | one line per hull class):

PRICING: a hull costs armour tonnage + PD turrets + weapon energy. Torpedoes are priced per round on delivered yield (18 GJ each at the 12 km/s closure floor, vs 4.3 GJ for a spinal coiler slug), so magazine depth is the single biggest line item on a torpedo hull. Saturation is buyable, but you pay for every round.

- corvette [24 pts] 3.0g, armor 212/36/42cm (nose/lat/tail), 1x PD laser, 8 torpedoes | 1x torpedo launcher | Torpedo Boat
- frigate [7 pts] 3.0g, armor 71/12/14cm (nose/lat/tail), 2x PD laser | 1x Coilgun Battery Mk3 (0.7 GJ muzzle) | Escort
- destroyer [18 pts] 2.0g, armor 151/26/30cm (nose/lat/tail), 2x PD laser | 1x Spinal Coiler Mk3 (4.3 GJ muzzle), 1x Coilgun Battery Mk3 (0.7 GJ muzzle) | Main Combat
- cruiser [29 pts] 1.5g, armor 241/41/48cm (nose/lat/tail), 2x PD laser | 1x Spinal Coiler Mk3 (4.3 GJ muzzle), 2x Coilgun Battery Mk3 (0.7 GJ muzzle) | Heavy Combatant
- battlecruiser [25 pts] 1.5g, armor 177/30/35cm (nose/lat/tail), 2x PD laser | 1x Spinal Coiler Mk3 (4.3 GJ muzzle), 2x Coilgun Battery Mk3 (0.7 GJ muzzle) | Fast Capital
- battleship [43 pts] 1.0g, armor 262/45/52cm (nose/lat/tail), 3x PD laser | 1x Spinal Coiler Mk3 (4.3 GJ muzzle), 3x Heavy Coilgun Battery Mk3 (1.2 GJ muzzle), 1x Coilgun Battery Mk3 (0.7 GJ muzzle) | Line of Battle
- dreadnought [55 pts] 0.75g, armor 251/43/50cm (nose/lat/tail), 4x PD laser | 1x Spinal Coiler Mk3 (4.3 GJ muzzle), 5x Heavy Coilgun Battery Mk3 (1.2 GJ muzzle), 1x Coilgun Battery Mk3 (0.7 GJ muzzle) | Mobile Fortress
- dreadnought_siege [56 pts] 0.676g, armor 251/43/50cm (nose/lat/tail), 4x PD laser | 1x Heavy Siege Coiler Mk3 (7.2 GJ muzzle), 5x Heavy Coilgun Battery Mk3 (1.2 GJ muzzle), 1x Coilgun Battery Mk3 (0.7 GJ muzzle) | Siege Platform
- cruiser_torpedo [100 pts] 1.5g, armor 241/41/48cm (nose/lat/tail), 4x PD laser, 48 torpedoes | 4x torpedo launcher | Torpedo cruiser. No guns: it closes under armor and delivers a saturation salvo. 4 launchers fire 8 torpedoes per 30s decision - enough to overwhelm a dreadnought's point defense and land the hits that kill it in one coordinated strike.

DOCTRINE NOTES:
- Coilguns: spinal mounts hit hard but need the nose on target; turrets cover
  the front hemisphere. Gun accuracy rises steeply as range drops below
  ~300 km.
- Torpedoes: 12g guided rounds. Point defense needs 3+ turrets dwelling on a
  round to blind its seeker, so SATURATION (many rounds arriving together)
  beats trickled launches. Rounds whose target dies mid-flight retarget a
  reachable enemy on their own (live seeker + fuel permitting; healthy
  seekers maximize impact energy, PD-singed ones race the fastest
  intercept before blinding). Torpedo hulls die fast if caught alone.
- Point defense also shaves incoming coilgun slugs. Ships with 3-4 PD turrets
  anchor a defensive wall.
- Fast light hulls (3g) can dictate range against slow capitals (<= 1g).

WEAPON EFFECTS (calibrated from recorded battles):
- ALL kinetic impacts scale with closing speed - gun GJ ratings are muzzle
  energy against a stationary target. Mutual closure multiplies them and
  mutual recession bleeds them off (measured: the same guns landed 0.2 to
  8.7 GJ per hit depending on encounter geometry). Coilgun rounds do NOT
  accelerate after launch - no guidance, so at long range an evading
  target simply is not where the slug arrives.
- Armor ablates at roughly 1.5 cm per GJ before anything penetrates.
  Noses carry 3-8x the armor of flanks and tails - kill ships by cracking
  a thin facing, then penetrating hits wreck modules (bridge, magazines,
  reactor).
- Torpedoes DO accelerate and steer all the way in (12g), so their closure
  scaling is one-sided in the attacker's favor: ~95 GJ against a head-on
  charge, ~23 GJ at zero closure, ~8 GJ chasing a receding ship - and a
  receding EVADING target usually escapes the round entirely.

TORPEDO FLIGHT PROFILE (what a defender exploits):
- Each round carries 14 km/s of delta-v at 12g (about two minutes of total
  burn) and flies augmented proportional navigation. It never brakes:
  braking would waste its own warhead. Outside its no-escape zone it
  spends only what steering demands - hoarding delta-v so it can reach
  the NEZ at all - and merely enforces a minimum cruise closure.
- The no-escape zone is its commit line: the round continuously checks
  whether your best full-lateral burn could still build miss distance
  faster than its remaining thrust authority and fuel can null. Once you
  cannot, it commits - dumping every spare m/s into MORE closing speed
  (impact energy scales as v^2, and a shorter run gives PD fewer dwell
  windows), holding back only a ~0.5 km/s reserve for final corrections.
- So the fight against a torpedo is won EARLY or not at all: hard evasion
  and low closure before the NEZ force it to burn its budget in the
  chase, and a dry round is a ballistic miss. PD blinding is inherently a
  terminal-window affair (laser coupling only bites in roughly the last
  110 km, by which point the round is usually committed) - PD thins
  salvos, it does not save a ship that let the geometry close.

TORPEDO COUNTERPLAY (seeded runs: a 4 battlecruiser + 2 destroyer + 2 frigate
gun wall against 5 corvettes + 3 frigates, 40 rounds):
- From 500 km a nose-on wall took 72% of the rounds (on the nose) and lost 6
  of 8 hulls; burning straight away it took 37% (on the thin tail, ~14% less
  energy each) and lost 5 of 8; charging it took 73% and lost all 8. From
  1000 km: nose-on lost 8 of 8, burning away 4 of 8, charging 3 of 8 (and
  killed 1.3 boats). Burning away leaves more rounds blinded or dry; what
  still hits lands on the tail. An emptied torpedo hull mounts no guns: it
  dies to whatever can catch it afterward.
- A fleet only kites as fast as its slowest hull. Mixing 3g screens with
  <=1g capitals means choosing between abandoning the capitals or eating
  the waves at capital speed - commit to one doctrine, not half of each.

Call select_fleet with your purchase. Spend your points well - unspent points
are wasted.

bceb25e08a2896f36fed3bcfe43967a6c14cb614.content: Buy your fleet now with select_fleet.

function.name: select_fleet
function.description: Buy your fleet from the catalog. Limits: total cost <= 150 points AND at most 8 hulls (the sum of all counts). Unspent points are wasted. You must buy at least one ship. Fill budget_check first, then ships with exactly the hulls you added up.

budget_check.description: Write this FIRST: every hull line with count x price, the point total and the hull count against the limits, e.g. '2 battleship 2x43=86 + 3 destroyer 3x18=54 = 140 of 150 points; 5 of 8 hulls'

ships.description: Hull classes and how many of each to buy (as in budget_check)

rationale.description: One or two sentences on the fleet concept

- TIS Ward-2 (frigate, 7 pts)

Now PLACE YOUR FORMATION. Coordinates are km offsets from your fleet anchor,
in YOUR frame: +x points AT the enemy, y is lateral (your left/right), z is
vertical. Offsets are limited to +/-150 km per axis; the
enemy fleet starts 500 km down the +x axis.

Considerations:
- Ships within ~100 km of each other can overlap PD coverage against torpedoes.
- A ship pushed +x is your vanguard (absorbs the first exchange); -x holds it
  back as a reserve or keeps a fragile torpedo hull out of gun range.
- Lateral/vertical spread complicates enemy spinal geometry but dilutes PD.

Call set_formation with a placement for each ship.

2615e86c54ccfbe4a63165b4b6851b92e81087c2.content: Place your formation now with set_formation.

function.name: set_formation
function.description: Place your drafted ships in their battle-start formation. Offsets are km from your fleet anchor in YOUR frame: +x points at the enemy fleet, y is lateral, z is vertical. Offsets are limited to +/-150 km per axis. Ships you do not place get default line-abreast slots.

formation_name.description: Short name for the formation (e.g. 'PD wall')

rationale.description: Why this shape (screening, PD overlap, flanking...)
